# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The baseline passes the frozen simulation and has routed timing slack of WNS 0.313 ns and WHS 0.153 ns. It uses 37 LUTs and 46 FFs on xc7a35tcpg236-1; with both designs timing-feasible, promotion requires a strict LUT reduction and all verification and metric gates to pass. The current top’s known latency is 9 cycles, so retain `// @latency 9` and its defined cycle behavior.

## Hypothesis
Sharing one subtract operation to produce both the trial remainder and the no-borrow decision may reduce LUT use by eliminating separate compare and subtract logic, while preserving the iterative divider’s behavior.

## Instruction for generator
In the trial-remainder arithmetic, replace the separate unsigned `>=` comparison and subtraction with one explicitly extended subtraction whose carry/no-borrow result selects between the original trial remainder and the difference. Keep the quotient-bit decision, iteration count, registered outputs, handshake, reset priority, and all cycle timing unchanged; retain `// @latency 9`. Preserve unsigned high-bit behavior, including divisor zero and the supported WIDTH cases 1, 2, 4, 8, 13, and 16. The expected benefit is fewer routed LUTs; accept only if the unchanged verification gates pass, routed setup and hold slack remain nonnegative, metrics are valid, and LUT use is strictly below 37.
